reason: The hypothesis relies on the formation of precipitates in CoCrFeNiTi upon aging, but none of the cited passages (E1, E2, E3) involve this specific alloy system. E1 shows precipitation strengthening in different MPEAs, E2 discusses L12 precipitates in an Al-containing eutectic HEA, and E3 concerns a non-equiatomic CoNiCrFeC alloy. No evidence is provided that equimolar CoCrFeNiTi forms nanoscale precipitates under the proposed conditions, leaving the central premise unsupported.
premises: Equimolar CoCrFeNiTi can be in a single-phase FCC solid-solution state with low hardness/strength.
Thermal aging at ~500°C can form nanoscale precipitates in this alloy.
These precipitates will be coherent or semi-coherent with the FCC matrix.
Nanoscale precipitates hinder dislocation motion, increasing hardness and yield strength.
The cited evidence supports precipitation strengthening in related high-entropy alloys.
